w: Bal - Balika National Convention Balaks and balikas had a chance to learn about Swamishri's travels for them, as the theme for the day was ‘Vicharan to My Heart’.

Swamishri demonstrated his efforts to make children happy when he arrived in the morning session by playing a game of pictionary with sadhus and balaks. Swamishri first served as judge, but then he himself drew pictures to give memories to the balaks and balikas. At the conclusion of the morning session, a question and answer session was held, during which Swamishri explained the importance of learning to speak, understand, read, and write Gujarati. He also described how children can serve their parents, primarily by behaving according to their parents’ wishes and by respecting them. Balaks presented a very creative evening programme, in which they entered a ‘time machine’. They went back in time to see first-hand what the time of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and his spiritual succession of God-realised Sadhus was like. They chose five different locations in time, starting with Bhagwan Swaminarayan's time, and moving all the way through to Yogiji Maharaj's time. At each place in time, they learned about incidents related to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the guru parampara through speeches, dramas, and dances. Sadhus also sang kirtans about Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj and Brahmswarup Yogiji Maharaj, which put Swamishri, sadhus, and the delegates in a very joyous and festive mood. Swamishri also narrated his favourite incidents of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Shastriji Maharaj, and explained the importance of following agna through an incident involving Bhagatji Maharaj.
Before Swamishri left the assembly, he personally served dudhpak to the sadhus, as Shastriji Maharaj's shraddh was symbolically celebrated. Then, senior sadhus served dudhpak to all the balaks.

As part of a children's camp, children were presenting a programme on stage. Through a time machine, the children went from the time of Gunatitanand Swami into the time of Bhagatji Maharaj. But surprise! Instead of four children, four middle aged men came out of the time machine. One's hair had turned white, another had gone bald, and the pyjamas and kurtas all four were wearing had become too short. Before the four had got over their surprise, two children came on stage and told two incidents of Bhagatji Maharaj: "Where are the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage?" and "The key to Akshardham has now been handed to Pragji." Swamishri too, narrowing his eyes, was listening to the children with great concentration.

Finally a child came and innocently asked Pramukh Swami Maharaj a question: "Swami Bapa! On the command of Gunatitanand Swami, Bhagatji went to call Girnar. That was fine, but it is a huge mountain. How could it come?"

Answering this childlike question, Swamishri said, "Bhagatji Maharaj had satsang from the beginning. Then he came to Junagadh for the company of Gunatitanand Swami. Hearing his talks, he became convinced of Maharaj's supremacy and that Gunatitanand Swami is Mul Akshar. These two things became firm, and he came to identify so completely with Swami that he obeyed every command Swami gave. He did not even have a second thought about his words.

"It is true that inanimate things do not come, but Bhagatji believed that whatever Swami said had divinity in it, that it was a true word. Bhagatji had the feeling that Gunatitanand Swami was the very incarnation of Akshar, and whatever he said was right, with no doubt about it. A true disciple has no doubt in the words of his guru.

"We should obey the commands and words of God and the Sant in this way. Whether the result comes or not, whether the work happens or not, that is up to their wish. If we have such firm faith, such trust and belief, God and the Sant are pleased."

In the evening Swamishri arrived at the musical fountain to inaugurate and perform the maha-arti of the 30-foot high murti of Neelkanth Varni. First Swamishri prayed for the welfare of all and performed pujan of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj. The pujari sanctified the maha-arti with Swamishri’s divine touch and then the arti “Jai Sadguru Swami…” was relayed on the public address system while Swamishri, senior sadhus and the pujari performed the maha-arti. Thousands in the audience, gathered for the fountain show, witnessed the devotional ritual. The maha-arti would be performed daily prior to the show.

Chandrakantbhai Birla, son of India's famous industrialist Gangaprasadji Birla, came for darshan today. He is the heir of the Birla Group, which for years dominated India's car industry by manufacturing the Ambassador car through Hindustan Motors, and even now he owns an empire of many businesses, including Hindustan Motors. As a social and spiritual service he is building Hindu temples, and he is also building many schools. He said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "You have done a very great service by building this Akshardham. Because of Akshardham, Hindu dharma is being hailed everywhere today. Otherwise, these days people are afraid in the name of religion and hold back."
Swamishri said, "We should do whatever we can for God, and for society and the poor too we should build universities, hospitals, everything."
He asked Swamishri for blessings that such good works would continue to be done through his family.

Because of Akshardham, today Hindu dharma is being hailed everywhere. Otherwise these days people are afraid in the name of religion and hold back."
Swamishri said, "Whatever can be done for Bhagwan should be done, and for society and the poor too, universities, hospitals, all these should be built."
He asked Swamishri for blessings that such good works continue to be done by his family.

The central theme of today's youth assembly was "Eva santne namu hu shish" (I bow my head to such a sadhu). When Mahant Swami Maharaj set out to go to the youth assembly, 2 staff from the Bartlett Fire Protection department and 3 from the Bartlett Police department were standing there for his darshan.

As soon as Swamishri arrived, all five of these officers offered him panchang pranam (bowing with five parts of the body touching the ground). It was a sight no one could have imagined! By bowing their heads to a true sadhu, these American devotees had, as it were, begun the youth assembly right there. Swamishri was very pleased. He gave all five of them blessings and prasad.

Swamishri went on ahead to the assembly, but tears came to the eyes of the fire protection chief, Shri Michael. Choked with emotion, he said, "We are very fortunate that we have had the good fortune to meet such a holy person, and we feel very humbled to have met him."

And the fire marshal, whose name was also Michael, said that on meeting Swamishri the hairs on his body stood on end. And the police officers said, "These were the best moments of our careers, which we will never be able to forget."
How can one on whom a shower of nectar falls remain without getting wet?

In today's evening assembly, youths were presenting their problems through skits, and Mahant Swami Maharaj was giving solutions. In it one problem was presented: "It is hard to keep a balance between mandir, home and work, so please bless us and tell us what we should do."

Swamishri said slowly, "You should become a sadhu." Then he burst out laughing. Then he said, "It is true, one who has it in his destiny becomes a sadhu. Hundreds of thousands of devotees were in family life, but they had firmly established their understanding: to please Shriji

Maharaj or to please their coworkers? Because in countless births we have taken, we have never had such an opportunity as meeting Shriji Maharaj. If we think like this, our whole attitude changes. It becomes filled with satsang. Then no problem remains. If in your mind it is clear that satsang is true and everything else is false, there will be no problem. What is done for the world will bear no fruit: zero. Satsang will bear fruit. The talk of satsang is true. So lean towards satsang. Mandir seva comes first. Otherwise there is no objection to jobs and business. Carry on as you are doing."
